title: Is RamosLabs indigo (#4f46e5) WCAG accessible?
summary: RamosLabs indigo #4f46e5 passes WCAG AA on white at 6.29:1 but not AAA, so use --color-primary-dark #4338ca when AAA is required.
short: Yes for AA. --color-primary #4f46e5 on white is 6.29:1, which passes the 4.5:1 threshold for normal text and the 3:1 threshold for UI components, but it does not reach AAA (7:1). When AAA is required, use --color-primary-dark #4338ca, which gives 7.90:1 with white text.

sections.heading: Indigo pairings and their contrast ratios
body: The table lists the indigo pairings in the RamosLabs DS contrast data, including the pairings that fail. Ratios use the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula and are rounded to two decimals.
--color-primary is #4f46e5, which is indigo 600 and the single action accent. --color-primary-dark is #4338ca, which is indigo 700 and is used for hover.

sections.heading: WCAG thresholds
body: WCAG 2.2 AA requires at least 4.5:1 for normal text and at least 3:1 for large text and UI components such as control edges and focus rings. AAA requires at least 7:1 for normal text.
The RamosLabs DS sets AA as its minimum. The primary indigo meets AA for text on white and on the primary surface. Reach AAA with the darker --color-primary-dark.
A pair that passes on one background can fail on another, so check each pair as it is used.

sections.heading: Primary button with a visible focus state
body: The snippet uses only RamosLabs token variables. The white label comes from --color-surface, which is #ffffff. The hover state switches to --color-primary-dark, and the focus state replaces the outline with --shadow-focus, which is a 2px white gap followed by a 4px #4f46e5 ring.
Import the token stylesheet once at the app entry before using these rules.

code.label: button.css

sections.heading: Recommended and avoid
body: ✓ Recommended: use white text on --color-primary for the primary button label, which is 6.29:1.
Rule: pair the button label with a token background that passes at least 4.5:1 for normal text.
Why: 6.29:1 passes AA, so the label remains readable for users with low vision, and the same pair is used in the snippet above.
✕ Avoid: indigo 300 #a5b4fc as text on white.
Rule: text colors must reach at least 4.5:1 on their background, and indigo 300 does not.
Why: indigo 300 on white is 1.99:1, which fails both the 4.5:1 text threshold and the 3:1 UI threshold.

sections.heading: Verify a pair with the MCP check_contrast tool
body: The RamosLabs DS MCP server exposes a check_contrast tool. The endpoint is https://design.ramoslabs.com/mcp. It uses Streamable HTTP, is read-only, and needs no auth.
To add the server to Claude Code, run: claude mcp add --transport http ramoslabs-ds https://ramoslabs-ds.edwardramosp.workers.dev/mcp
Pass the foreground and background pair to check_contrast and read the result it returns. This page does not describe the output format of the tool, so check the response directly.

faq.q: Is #4f46e5 accessible on a white background?
faq.a: Yes for WCAG 2.x AA. The contrast ratio is 6.29:1, which clears 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for UI components. It does not reach the AAA threshold of 7:1 for normal text.

faq.q: Can I use indigo 300 for text on white?
faq.a: No. Indigo 300 #a5b4fc on white is 1.99:1, which fails both the 4.5:1 text threshold and the 3:1 UI threshold.

faq.q: Which indigo should I use when AAA is required?
faq.a: Use --color-primary-dark #4338ca. White text on it is 7.90:1, which passes AAA for normal text. The primary #4f46e5 reaches 6.29:1 on white and does not reach AAA.

faq.q: Can I put white text on the primary button?
faq.a: Yes. White on --color-primary #4f46e5 is 6.29:1, which passes AA. For AAA, use white on --color-primary-dark #4338ca, which is 7.90:1.

faq.q: Does the primary indigo have enough contrast for a focus ring?
faq.a: Yes. Primary on white is 6.29:1, which clears the 3:1 threshold for UI component edges. The focus state uses --shadow-focus, which is a 2px white gap and a 4px #4f46e5 ring.

faq.q: How can I check a color pair programmatically?
faq.a: Use the check_contrast tool on the RamosLabs DS MCP server at https://design.ramoslabs.com/mcp. The server is read-only, uses Streamable HTTP, and needs no auth.
